subject: Transient 5xx surge from rw-7b-quant — customer impact, mitigation and recovery
messages:
From: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@helios.health>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Health Platform Team <platform@helios.health>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: latency and 5xx errors seen on model rw-7b-quant this morning

Hi Soojin —

We started seeing a bump in 500s around 07:50 PST this morning when routing to rw-7b-quant for our batch scoring. Spike lasted ~25 minutes; a small percentage of requests returned 5xx and several timed out. We captured a sample of failed request IDs and included a small query set (attached). Can you confirm if this was on your side and whether a rollback or variant routing is in place? Our production SLA window is sensitive, so any context appreciated.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Grant
Engineering Lead, Integrations
Helios Health

Attachments: sample-queries-helio.csv
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@helios.health>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: latency and 5xx errors seen on model rw-7b-quant this morning

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the samples. We observed an elevated 5xx rate and timeouts from the rw-7b-quant variant during the 07:45–08:10 PST window. Impact looks concentrated on batch scoring routes that prefer the quantized variant.

Immediate actions we took:
- Switched traffic for your production route to rw-7b-fp16 (compatible variant) at 08:02 PST to avoid further user-visible errors.
- Throttled concurrent batch workers that were exceeding typical token concurrency.
- Collected KV cache and kernel traces for the window (attaching the relevant error log).

We're working a root-cause analysis; preliminary signals point to a kernel selection path that under certain sequence-length distributions hit a degraded quantized kernel on specific GPU drivers. Marcus and Hannah are digging in.

I'll update you as we confirm the root cause and any follow-up mitigations. Sorry for the disruption — we routed to a fully compatible variant to restore success rates.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: error_log-rw7b-2026-04-09.txt
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: kernel selection trace for rw-7b-quant 07:45 window (internal)

Forwarding internal trace summary —

On Thu Apr 9 08:03:10 PST the runtime selected an alternate int8-quant kernel due to a sequence-length heuristic for requests >512 tokens in a single batch. Under driver version 510.47, the kernel fell back to a slow path which intermittently returned 5xx due to an unhandled memory stride check.

What we validated so far:
- Reproduced failure on a repro cluster with 510.47 drivers and identical seq-length distribution.
- No failures observed on 525.xx drivers or with fp16 variant.
- The quant kernel has a race in the stride check when batching mixes short and long sequences.

Mitigations implemented:
- Automated routing rule added to prefer fp16 for routes with >15% long-sequence traffic (applied to Helios route at 08:02 PST).
- Hotfix queued to adjust kernel stride check for next runtime roll (SUP-4892).
- Temporary guard: disable int8-quant kernel on nodes running 510.47 until kernel patch lands.

Will coordinate rollback plan if we need to revert any of these changes.

—Marcus
Principal Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@helios.health>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: latency and 5xx errors seen on model rw-7b-quant this morning

Hi all —

Quick update for Helios: We rolled out the guard (disabled int8-quant on affected driver pool) across the US region at 08:30 PST and confirmed error rates returned to baseline by 08:40. I followed up with an automated smoke run against your sample set and full production mimic; all requests completed successfully against rw-7b-fp16.

Next steps and timeline:
- Engineering will land the kernel fix in the runtime branch by Tue 2026-04-14 (SUP-4892) and run a staged canary across updated nodes.
- We'll coordinate a safe re-enable of int8-quant after the canary completes and after we validate driver interactions.
- I'll send a postmortem with root cause analysis, timeline, and recommended customer actions (if any) by Wed 2026-04-15.

Jordan, please confirm we added Helios to the impacted-customers list for the upcoming postmortem and that we have a single POC for remediation communication.

Thanks —
Hannah
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@helios.health>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Health Platform Team <platform@helios.health>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: latency and 5xx errors seen on model rw-7b-quant this morning

Thank you — this was helpful and the switch to fp16 stabilized our pipelines. Please include any recommended changes on our side (e.g., driver pinning or routing rules) in the postmortem; we want to avoid surprises in scheduled overnight batch runs. We'll keep our teams on standby for any canary notifications.

Appreciate the quick action and the log/trace details.

Best,
Alyssa
Engineering Lead, Integrations
Helios Health
